story.iWant: drag clips to reorder them on the timeline
story.soThat: I can arrange my video sequence in any order
story.tasks: - Add reorderClips action to timelineStore (reorder array, recalculate startTime) - Implement drag handlers in TimelineClip component (draggable, onDragStart/End) - Implement drop target logic in Timeline component (calculate drop position) - Add visual feedback during drag operation (ghost, drop indicator) - Recalculate timeline after reorder (sequential startTime updates) - Update preview player for reordered sequence (test playback) - Handle edge cases for drag-to-reorder - Test drag-to-reorder functionality end-to-end

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: AC1: User can click and drag a timeline clip to a new position AC2: Clips automatically shift to make space during drag operation AC3: Drop clip between other clips to insert at that position AC4: Timeline updates time markers after reordering AC5: Preview updates to show reordered sequence during playback AC6: Drag operation is smooth with visual feedback (ghost/preview)

docs.doc: Drag-to-reorder allows clip repositioning. Visual feedback shows drop target. Clips array reordered, then startTime recalculated sequentially. Must maintain 30fps smooth animation per NFR001.
User drags clip → Timeline calculates drop index → Visual feedback shows drop target → On drop → reorderClips(sourceIndex, destIndex) → Store reorders array → Timeline re-renders.
Timeline components in src/renderer/components/Timeline/. TimelineClip.tsx handles drag handlers. Timeline.tsx handles drop targets. State mutations in timelineStore.ts.
Application shall support multi-clip arrangement on timeline with drag-to-reorder functionality. NFR001: Timeline UI shall maintain 30+ fps responsiveness.

frameworks.framework: UI framework with TypeScript, HTML5 drag-and-drop API
Styling for drag ghost and drop indicator

constraints.constraint: Zustand immutability: reorderClips creates new clips array, recalculates startTime for all clips
NFR001: Drag operation must maintain 30fps smooth animation using CSS transitions (not JS animations)
Renderer-only operation: No IPC calls, pure state mutation in renderer process
Use HTML5 native drag-and-drop API (draggable attribute, onDragStart/onDrop events)
After reorder, clips must be sequentially positioned (no gaps): Clip N startTime = sum of all previous clip durations

tests.standards: Use Vitest testing framework. Unit tests for reorderClips action in timelineStore.test.ts. Test array reordering immutability, startTime recalculation. Use describe/it/expect pattern. Manual testing for drag-and-drop UI interactions.

ideas.idea: Manual test: Click and drag a clip → verify draggable attribute works, cursor changes to "grabbing"
Manual test: During drag, verify visual feedback (ghost clip, drop indicator line)
Test reorderClips: [A, B, C], move C to position 0 → result [C, A, B]
Test reorderClips: [A, B, C], move A to position 2 → result [B, C, A]
Test startTime recalculation after reorder: verify sequential positioning (Clip 0 at 0s, Clip 1 at Clip 0 duration, etc.)
Manual test: Reorder clips, then play timeline → verify preview plays in new sequence
Performance test: Drag clip rapidly → verify smooth 30fps animation, no jank
Test reorder with only 2 clips → verify positions swap correctly
Test drag clip to same position (sourceIndex === destIndex) → verify no state update (no-op)
Test reorder with trimmed clips → verify effective duration used for positioning
